<description>
This PR introduces a new `libbitcoin_kernel` internal library. It completes the internal library design as laid out in [doc/design/libraries.md](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/blob/master/doc/design/libraries.md). Since the `util` library contains a bunch of modules that are not required by the kernel library, a new `kernel_util` library is introduced as well that only consists of the modules required by the kernel library. The external `libbitcoinkernel` library now re-uses the compiled objects from the internal libraries.

There is a trade-off to this. Since we don't manually export symbols from the kernel library yet, this would make the library unusable if `REDUCE_EXPORTS=ON`. For now this means that the patch here introduces a separate source file list for the external library that gets populated by the source files of its static dependents.
</description>

[2026-09-18] rc:4048632873 inline on src/util/CMakeLists.txt by stickies-v (member) (edited 2026-09-18):
I think libraries should be organized around what contents they have, not around who consumes or mustn't consume them. The consumer-oriented approach makes for libraries that don't feel natural and encourage kitchen-sink behaviour.

If a consumer requires some capabilities from a library but definitely shouldn't have access to other capabilities in that same library, we should take that as a signal to split the library into two smaller, logically coherent libraries.

Instead of floating further in the direction of consumer-oriented library organization, with libraries like `util_kernel` or `kernel_lite`, I think we can and should move towards a more natural library organization in this PR, without adding scope creep.

For example, in [this branch](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/compare/master...stickies-v:bitcoin:2026-09/kernel-content-libs) I've (LLM) prototyped an approach where we add `chain`, `policy`, `validation, `net` and `system` libraries`, plus a `bitcoin_kernel` CMake INTERFACE target that just names the kernel's member libraries and compiles nothing. Of course, some files are still in a library that doesn't match their content (e.g. `policy/rbf.cpp` in `validation` instead of `policy`), but that can be improved over time as we improve decoupling. It also adds a few (6, I believe) more `util` files back into the kernel library that `master`'s kernel list doesn't compile (like `util/string.cpp`), but I think when we organize libraries by contents instead of consumers that is inevitable - and fine?

With the approach in my branch, I really like that there is:
- no dependency on `kernel` by `wallet` and `common`
- no consumer-defined libraries like `util_kernel` or `kernel_lite` that feel awkward
- a path towards increasingly removing stuff from `util` and `common`, which should never have gotten as big as they are
